newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO police turn back demonstrators in Ramallah.
newsitem.headline: PLO police turn back demonstrators in Ramallah.

text.p: Yasser Arafat's elite security forces held back stone-throwing Palestinian demonstrators from an Israeli checkpoint near Ramallah on Thursday as Israeli tanks rolled outside the Palestinian-ruled area, witnesses said.
"Two hours ago we received clear instructions not to fire any shots unless in self-defence," Jihad al-Ghoul, head of Force 17 in the Palestinian President's office, told Reuters.

Witnesses said all of Arafat's bodyguards were in Ramallah, the site of two days of fierce clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops which have left 33 Palestinians and five Israelis dead in running gunbattles across the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Israel rolled out tanks near a checkpoint in an Israeli-controled area and a Palestinian security officer reported Israelis were trying to calm the unrest.

An Israeli helicopter circled overhead. Israeli soldiers earlier fired from two helicopters at police on top of apartment houses near Ramallah. Jewish settlers also opened fire in Ramallah, witnesses said.
Palestinian police formed a human chain in an attempt to hold back hundreds of youths throwing stones and bottles at Israeli soldiers manning a checkpoint south of the Ramallah self-rule enclave.
Witnesses said demonstrators tried to outflank police and push through their lines but were turned back.
The head of Force 17 in Ramallah appealed to demonstrators to go home, saying that "victory" had been won.

"We want to invest in the victory of what happened yesterday and today. We must give negotiations now a chance. There are contacts now betweeen the two sides on Hebron and Jerusalem. Please go back to your homes," Akeed Abu Fakhr announced from a loudspeaker in his car.

In self-ruled Nablus, Palestinian police closed off the area around the shrine of the biblical Joseph's Tomb, which Palestinian demonstrators were attacking, a Palestinian official said. Israel Radio reported two Israelis were killed at the site on Thursday.
Israel Radio reported fierce fighting at the tomb.
